scenario: [LEXP.3.7.1]: `x.bit_count` counts the 1 bits of the 64-bit two's-complement pattern, so -1 has 64 and INT64_MIN has 1. It is not Python's `int.bit_count`, which counts the magnitude's bits and gives 1 for -1. Rule `counted` fires where `t.x.bit_count` equals the fact's `want`; the receiver is an `Int` slot. PATH PINNED: FN_BIT_COUNT in libds (`builtins.c`, `__builtin_popcountll` over the unsigned pattern) and Mercury (`ds.eval`, `u64_ones`).
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    id: String key
    x: Int mutable
    want: Int mutable

rule counted:
    T t where t.x.bit_count == t.want
->
    log info "counted {t.id}"
